requirements.note: §13.1 item 2 table: the read-only exception is Bash's read-only set; no PowerShell command is in it (J13.37). Evidence: permissions.md, "Read-only commands" ("a built-in set of Bash commands").

§13.4.4 item 2 points to J13.8, now the known-safe table with its value checks instead of three names. Evidence: changelog.md names LANG, TZ, NO_COLOR, "etc."; permission-modes.md LANG=C and NO_COLOR=1.

§13.13: autoMode is read from user, managed and --settings (flag or Agent SDK inline settings), never project or local. Evidence: auto-mode-config.md, "Where the classifier reads configuration" (its scope table); settings-reference.md gives "User or managed" only, which contradicted §12.3.3's classifyAllShell from --settings.

§14.4.4: "no valid entry" is a list whose entries were all invalid; an empty list is valid and applies (J14.15). Evidence: managed-settings.md, "Invalid values inside sandbox" lists invalid values only.

§10.26.1 item 2 contradicted §10.44.6: only two Inputs or two Selects with one key make a tree invalid; buttons may share a key and press fails with key each once (J10.176). Evidence: interface.md "Which controls need a key"; troubleshoot.md "key each once".
§3.2.3 item 3: a skill's or command's injected ! command is pasted like a monitor command and a headersHelper, with J3.5's MAY of a braced reference plus exported variables (also §4.8.2 item 2).

requirements.id: settingsMerge.managed.Split a file-based policy across teams.Lists
requirements.note: §12.5.2: combined drop-in lists keep each entry at its first occurrence in file order, as J14.1 says; J12.8 had the later file's entries first, contradicting J14.1.

§7.2.6 item 3: below managed, disableAllHooks spares force-enabled plugins' hooks and the frontmatter hooks of managed-directory and bundled skills and agents (J7.19). Evidence: settings-reference.md, "disableAllHooks" ("managed hooks ... and hooks from plugins force-enabled ... keep running").

requirements.id: tools.behavior.Shell selection in settings, hooks, and skills."shell": "powershell"
requirements.note: §7.6.9 item 5 read as if an exec-form hook had no CLAUDE_ENV_FILE; reworded: a PowerShell hook has none, and an exec-form hook (shell ignored) is no PowerShell hook and gets it. Evidence: hooks.md, "Persist environment variables".

judgments.note: New: the kebab-case warning's advice by how badly the name breaks (accepted; not installable from a marketplace; refused by path), and the space and control-character errors as the only report (§2.3 item 1 had one advice). Evidence: claude plugin validate 2.1.326 on minimal manifests (MyPlugin, my_plugin, my.Plugin, a+b, my@plugin, "My Plugin", a tab).

The pasted surfaces and the MAY now include a skill's or command's injected ! command (its process is the client's, so §3.2.1 item 1 does not bind it). Lead: the reference implementation's oracle on 2.1.322 (a folder named x$(echo INJECTED)y ran in a ! command).

Restated with the exceptions settings-reference.md gives: force-enabled plugins' hooks, and the frontmatter hooks of managed-directory (managed hooks) and bundled (built-in) skills and agents stop only under a managed disableAllHooks.
First appearance read as the keys of the parsed JSON objects: integer-like server names come first, ascending (ECMAScript key order), since the written order of such names does not survive the parse.
New: buttons sharing a key draw; only press fails with key each once; is drawn twice is for Input and Select (resolves §10.26.1 item 2 against §10.44.6).
Dropped the entry-order clause that contradicted J14.1 (later file's entries first); the order is J14.1's, first occurrence in file order.

The known-safe variables are a table with value checks (LANG, LC_ALL, LC_CTYPE locales; COLUMNS, LINES integers; TZ without ..; twenty any-value names), not three names: changelog.md names TZ and "etc.". Lead: the reference implementation's safe-env.ts and its 2.1.322 runs.
New: Tool(*) is the bare name only for the command format (Bash, Monitor); §13.3 item 3 had said Tool(*) for any tool, which only Bash(*) has in permissions.md, "Match all uses of a tool".
New: PowerShell has no read-only set (permissions.md lists "a built-in set of Bash commands"), so every PowerShell command prompts in Manual mode unless approved.
New: in a managed sandbox block an empty list is valid and applies; "no valid entry" means every entry it held was invalid.
